title: A redelivered overdraft was counted twice
detail: The log delivers at least once, so a consumer restart redelivers events. State and the lake both counted the second copy. The processor now remembers processed event ids and drops repeats, counting them for the report.

title: A late older payment overwrote a newer one
detail: Within a month the processor kept whichever payment, credit or alt-data event arrived last. A late older event replaced newer days past due. State now keeps the event with the newest event time.

title: Offsets were committed before processing, so a crash lost events
detail: The consumer committed its offset on poll. A crash after the poll and before processing skipped those events forever. Offsets are now committed only after the batch is published and applied.

title: A renamed field loaded as zero and a null borrower created a ghost borrower
detail: The upstream servicer renamed days_past_due to dpd with no version bump, which loaded as zero days late, and events without a borrower id created a ghost borrower. Every event is validated against a contract, violations go to a dead-letter table, a drift alarm fires, and confirmed aliases can be replayed.

title: A retried batch was stored twice
found: retry test on the Iceberg writer
detail: A batch that failed after writing was written again on retry. Each batch is now staged in its own table, audited, then published once, keyed by a batch id stored as a snapshot property.

title: Features for an earlier month changed when later months arrived
detail: Training features read the latest state, so the future leaked into the past. Features are now built only from months up to the as-of month.

title: A very late event changed state without reaching the lake
detail: Events beyond the allowed lateness still changed in-memory state, and a failed audit still changed state. They are parked in the dead-letter table and state is applied only after the lake publish.

title: A borrower above the threshold was alerted every month
detail: The same high-risk borrower was re-alerted each month, flooding the outreach queue. Repeat alerts are suppressed for 60 days unless days past due rises by 30 or more.

title: The model used a ZIP-level area risk feature, a geographic proxy
detail: Area risk by ZIP can act as a proxy for redlining. The feature was removed and a test now fails if any geographic feature returns. Scores use only borrower finances and loan terms.

title: A future-dated event pushed the watermark and every later event was dropped as late
detail: One bad timestamp moved the watermark far ahead, so real events looked late. Events more than 62 days ahead of the watermark are quarantined.

title: Training labeled unfinished windows as negatives
detail: Borrower-months whose 180 day window had not closed were counted as non-foreclosures, which biased the model. Training uses matured windows only, and the alert threshold is set without labels from the top 1.5 percent of the latest month.

title: SQL months shifted with the session time zone
detail: The dbt overdraft model cast event time in the session time zone, America/Chicago, so events near month boundaries landed in a different month than the processor's UTC buckets. 646 of 22,442 borrower-months disagreed. Months are now bucketed in UTC and the reconciliation shows zero mismatches.
